subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 07, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 07, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We're excited to share the latest updates from the world of AcreetionOS. First and foremost, we'd like to thank BetaNews for featuring AcreetionOS in their recent article, highlighting its ease of use and user-friendly interface. The article has been well-received by the community, and we're thrilled to see more people discovering the benefits of our Linux distribution.

In other news, Phoronix has published a performance benchmark comparison between Arch Linux, CachyOS, and Omarchy 4.5. While the results are interesting, we're proud to say that AcreetionOS remains a top choice for those seeking a stable and user-friendly Linux experience.

Unfortunately, a recent security alert has been circulating regarding fake Arch Linux packages that can push malware with root privileges. We urge all users to exercise caution when downloading software from unknown sources and to only use trusted repositories.

On a more positive note, videos from the XDC 2026 conference are now available online. We encourage you to check them out and stay up-to-date with the latest developments in the Linux community.

In terms of AcreetionOS development, we've made some significant progress in recent days. Our commit logs show a flurry of activity, including updates to our newsletter, archive, wiki guides, and feed. We're working hard to ensure that our distribution remains stable and user-friendly.

One commit in particular caught our eye: a fix for the postinstall.sh script that was silently failing on pwfeedback sudoers edit. This should improve the overall user experience for those using our Xlibre edition.

We've also seen some exciting developments in our community, including the creation of new wallpapers for our Carousel feature. Keep an eye out for these in the coming weeks.

As always, we appreciate your continued support and feedback. If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out to us on our Discord server or through our contact channels.

Finally, we'd like to remind you that our GitLab instance is available for all community members to use. Whether you're a developer or just looking for a place to collaborate, we invite you to join us and contribute to the AcreetionOS project.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're excited to see what the future holds for our distribution and look forward to continuing to work together to make Linux more accessible and user-friendly for all.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
